research_integrity.notes: Facts are drawn only from the local NAO, DHSC/CIO, CISA/US-CERT, and Microsoft MS17-010 sources listed in source_manifest.json. NHS impact counts prefer NAO where available.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NAO describes the 12 May 2017 incident as a global ransomware attack known as WannaCry that affected the NHS.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS Digital told NAO the majority of infected NHS devices were unpatched but on supported Microsoft Windows 7.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NAO records that unsupported XP devices were in the minority of identified infection issues.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NAO says managing firewalls facing the internet would have guarded organisations against infection whether patched or not.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS Digital confirmed WannaCry spread via the internet, including the N3 network.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS Digital confirmed there were no instances of the ransomware spreading via NHSmail.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NAO says the Department had no formal mechanism before 12 May to assess local compliance with its cyber advice.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS England data analysed by NAO showed at least 80 of 236 trusts across England were affected.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.object: 603 primary care and other NHS organisations
facts.evidence: NAO reports that a further 603 primary care and other NHS organisations were infected.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS England identified 6,912 cancelled appointments during its incident data collection.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: At 4 pm on 12 May, NHS England declared the cyber attack a major incident and implemented emergency arrangements.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: On the evening of 12 May a cyber-security researcher activated a kill-switch so WannaCry stopped locking devices.

facts.subject: WannaCry ransomware
facts.evidence: CISA describes the first WannaCry file as a dropper that contains and runs the ransomware.

facts.subject: WannaCry dropper
facts.evidence: CISA says the dropper propagated via the MS17-010/EternalBlue SMBv1.0 exploit.

facts.subject: MS17-010/EternalBlue SMBv1 exploit
facts.evidence: CISA states the malware propagated by exploiting the SMBv1 vulnerability documented by Microsoft bulletin MS17-010.

facts.subject: MS17-010/EternalBlue SMBv1 exploit
facts.evidence: CISA says initial reports indicated access through exploitation of a critical Windows SMB vulnerability.

facts.subject: Microsoft SMBv1 vulnerability
facts.evidence: Microsoft says the vulnerabilities involved Microsoft Server Message Block 1.0 (SMBv1) server.

facts.subject: Microsoft Windows SMBv1 server
facts.evidence: Microsoft states the most severe vulnerability could allow remote code execution.

facts.subject: Vulnerable to remote code execution
facts.evidence: Remote code execution could occur if an attacker sent specially crafted messages to an SMBv1 server.

facts.subject: Specially crafted SMBv1 messages
facts.evidence: Microsoft says the update corrected how SMBv1 handles specially crafted requests.

facts.subject: SMBv1 crafted-request handling
facts.evidence: The security update addresses the vulnerabilities by correcting SMBv1 handling of crafted requests.

facts.subject: Corrected SMBv1 request handling
facts.evidence: Microsoft Security Bulletin MS17-010 is the security update that resolves the SMBv1 vulnerabilities.

facts.subject: Microsoft SMBv1 vulnerability
facts.evidence: MS17-010 resolves vulnerabilities in Microsoft Windows SMB Server.

facts.subject: Microsoft Security Bulletin MS17-010
facts.evidence: The Microsoft bulletin states it was published on March 14, 2017.

facts.subject: Microsoft Security Bulletin MS17-010
facts.evidence: Microsoft titled MS17-010 as Critical and rated the update Critical for supported Windows releases.

facts.subject: Microsoft Security Bulletin MS17-010
facts.evidence: The affected software table repeatedly lists Critical Remote Code Execution for supported releases.

facts.subject: CISA TA17-132A alert
facts.evidence: The CISA/US-CERT alert is the 12 May 2017 TA17-132A WannaCry alert.

facts.subject: CISA TA17-132A alert
facts.evidence: CISA recommends applying the Microsoft patch for the MS17-010 SMB vulnerability dated March 14, 2017.

facts.subject: CISA TA17-132A alert
facts.object: Disable SMBv1 if patch cannot be applied
facts.evidence: CISA recommends considering disabling SMBv1 if the patch cannot be applied.

facts.subject: CISA TA17-132A alert
facts.object: Block SMB at the network boundary
facts.evidence: CISA recommends blocking SMB at the network boundary if patching cannot be applied.

facts.subject: Block SMB at the network boundary
facts.object: TCP port 445 and UDP 137-138 plus TCP 139
facts.evidence: CISA specifies blocking TCP port 445 with related UDP ports 137-138 and TCP port 139.

facts.subject: WannaCry dropper
facts.evidence: CISA reports the dropper attempts connections using UDP 137 and 138 and TCP 139 and 445.

facts.subject: WannaCry dropper
facts.object: Terminated if hard-coded URI connection succeeded
facts.evidence: CISA says the dropper attempts to connect to a hard-coded URI and terminates if the connection is established.

facts.subject: Majority unpatched Windows 7 devices
facts.evidence: NAO records that the majority of infected devices were unpatched but on supported Microsoft Windows 7.

facts.subject: Majority unpatched Windows 7 devices
facts.evidence: Trusts using Windows 7 could have protected themselves by applying the March 2017 Microsoft patch.

facts.subject: Majority unpatched Windows 7 devices
facts.evidence: Infected organisations had unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems; Windows 7 systems could have been protected by the March patch.

facts.subject: Unsupported Windows XP minority issues
facts.evidence: Microsoft was no longer releasing patches for Windows XP.

facts.subject: Unsupported Windows XP minority issues
facts.object: About 5 percent of NHS IT estate on 12 May 2017
facts.evidence: The Department told NAO that about 5% of the NHS IT estate still used Windows XP on 12 May 2017.

facts.subject: About 5 percent of NHS IT estate on 12 May 2017
facts.evidence: The 5% Windows XP estate included computers and medical equipment.

facts.subject: Computers and medical equipment
facts.evidence: NAO cites medical equipment such as MRI scanners with Windows XP embedded.

facts.subject: MRI scanners
facts.evidence: Trusts running Windows XP on medical equipment could have protected themselves by isolating devices from the rest of the network.

facts.subject: Isolating devices from the network
facts.evidence: NAO notes that isolating Windows XP medical equipment may necessitate manual workarounds.

facts.subject: Manual workarounds
facts.evidence: Some disrupted trusts used manual workarounds and recorded information using pen and paper.

facts.subject: Pen and paper records
facts.object: Used by 46 disrupted but not infected trusts
facts.evidence: NAO describes manual workarounds in disrupted trusts and separately counts 46 affected trusts that were not infected.

facts.subject: Used by 46 disrupted but not infected trusts
facts.object: Shutting down devices as a precaution
facts.evidence: The 46 non-infected disrupted trusts included organisations that shut down devices or systems as a precaution.

facts.subject: Shutting down devices as a precaution
facts.object: Absence of timely central advice early on 12 May
facts.evidence: NAO says some trusts took precautionary actions on their own initiative because they had not received central advice early enough on 12 May.

facts.subject: Unsupported Windows XP minority issues
facts.object: Microsoft Windows XP emergency patch after WannaCry
facts.evidence: Immediately after WannaCry, Microsoft issued a Windows XP patch that would prevent WannaCry and similar ransomware.

facts.subject: Internet-facing firewall management
facts.evidence: NAO says firewall management would have guarded organisations against infection whether patched or not.

facts.subject: WannaCry infection even when unpatched
facts.object: Unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems
facts.evidence: All NHS organisations infected by WannaCry had unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems.

facts.subject: Internet including the N3 network
facts.evidence: NAO states the internet route included the N3 network.

facts.subject: N3 network
facts.evidence: NAO describes N3 as the broadband network connecting all NHS sites in England.

facts.subject: All NHS sites in England
facts.evidence: Local health organisations connected into NHS services include trusts, GPs, CCGs and social care providers.

facts.subject: Local NHS organisations
facts.evidence: NAO lists NHS trusts and GPs among local organisations responsible for managing cyber-security.

facts.subject: No spread via NHSmail
facts.evidence: NAO says there were no instances of WannaCry spreading via NHSmail, the NHS email system.

facts.subject: NHSmail
facts.evidence: NAO identifies NHSmail as the NHS email system.

facts.subject: National NHS IT systems managed by NHS Digital
facts.evidence: NAO gives NHSmail as an example of a national system managed by NHS Digital.

facts.subject: National NHS IT systems managed by NHS Digital
facts.evidence: NAO gives the NHS Spine as an example of a national system managed by NHS Digital.

facts.subject: National NHS IT systems managed by NHS Digital
facts.evidence: NHS Digital told NAO that national NHS IT systems managed by NHS Digital were not infected.

facts.subject: NHS Spine
facts.evidence: The NHS Spine is included among national systems that NHS Digital told NAO were not infected.

facts.subject: NHS Spine
facts.object: Secure demographic and clinical information service
facts.evidence: NAO describes the Spine as holding secure demographic and clinical information.

facts.subject: Department of Health
facts.evidence: Before 12 May, the Department had no formal mechanism for assessing local compliance with its advice and guidance.

facts.subject: Department of Health
facts.evidence: The Department has overall national responsibility for cyber-security resilience and incident response in health.

facts.subject: Department of Health
facts.evidence: The Department and NHS England worked with NHS Digital and others to respond to the attack.

facts.subject: Department of Health
facts.evidence: NAO describes the Department and NHS England working together on the response.

facts.subject: Department of Health
facts.evidence: The Department and Cabinet Office wrote to trusts in 2014 about migrating from old software.

facts.subject: Cabinet Office
facts.evidence: The Department and Cabinet Office wrote to trusts in 2014 about robust plans to migrate away from Windows XP.

facts.subject: 2014 Windows XP migration letter
facts.object: Robust plans to migrate away from Windows XP
facts.evidence: The 2014 letter said robust plans to migrate away from old software such as Windows XP were essential.

facts.subject: Robust plans to migrate away from Windows XP
facts.evidence: The 2014 letter described temporary help until April 2015, after which there would be no support.

facts.subject: NHS Digital
facts.object: CareCERT alerts of March and April 2017
facts.evidence: NHS Digital issued critical alerts in March and April 2017 warning organisations to patch systems to prevent WannaCry.

facts.subject: CareCERT alerts of March and April 2017
facts.evidence: The CareCERT alerts asked trusts to apply the Microsoft patch issued in March 2017.

facts.subject: CareCERT alerts of March and April 2017
facts.evidence: NAO records CareCERT alerts on 17 March and 28 April asking organisations to apply the patch.

facts.subject: CareCERT alerts of March and April 2017
facts.evidence: NAO defines a CareCERT alert as an email from NHS Digital providing information or requiring action.

facts.subject: NHS Digital
facts.evidence: Before the attack, NHS Digital had conducted on-site cyber-security assessments for trusts.

facts.subject: CareCERT Assure assessments
facts.evidence: NHS Digital offered voluntary on-site CareCERT Assure inspections before the attack.

facts.subject: CareCERT Assure assessments
facts.evidence: The CareCERT Assure inspection assessed hospital cyber-security.

facts.subject: Voluntary on-site cyber-security inspections
facts.evidence: By 12 May, NHS Digital had inspected 88 of 236 trusts.

facts.subject: CareCERT Assure assessments
facts.evidence: NAO reports that NHS Digital inspected 88 of 236 trusts before the attack.

facts.subject: 88 of 236 trusts
facts.evidence: NAO says none of the 88 inspected trusts had passed.

facts.subject: None passed
facts.evidence: The none-passed result refers to assessments completed before 12 May 2017.

facts.subject: Before 12 May 2017
facts.evidence: NAO states that before 12 May 2017 the Department had no formal local compliance assessment mechanism.

facts.subject: Formal local cyber-compliance assessment mechanism
facts.evidence: The missing formal mechanism would have assessed whether organisations complied with cyber advice and guidance such as CareCERT alerts.

facts.subject: CareCERT alert compliance assurance
facts.object: CareCERT alerts of March and April 2017
facts.evidence: The relevant advice included NHS Digital's March and April 2017 CareCERT patch alerts.

facts.subject: NHS Digital
facts.object: Power to mandate local remedial action
facts.evidence: NAO says NHS Digital cannot mandate a local body to take remedial action.

facts.subject: NHS Digital
facts.object: High Severity CareCERT alert on 12 May 2017
facts.evidence: The DHSC lessons review says NHS Digital issued a High Severity CareCERT alert on 12 May.

facts.subject: High Severity CareCERT alert on 12 May 2017
facts.evidence: The DHSC review dates the High Severity CareCERT alert to 12 May 2017.

facts.subject: At least 80 of 236 trusts
facts.evidence: Of the 80 affected trusts, 34 were infected and locked out of devices.

facts.subject: At least 80 of 236 trusts
facts.evidence: NAO separately counts 46 trusts that were not infected but reported disruption.

facts.subject: At least 80 of 236 trusts
facts.object: At least 34 percent of trusts in England
facts.evidence: NAO says the attack led to disruption in at least 34% of trusts in England.

facts.subject: 34 infected and locked-out trusts
facts.evidence: The 34 infected locked-out trusts included 25 acute trusts.

facts.subject: 34 infected and locked-out trusts
facts.evidence: Infected trusts experienced medical equipment and devices being locked or isolated from IT systems.

facts.subject: Locked or isolated medical devices
facts.evidence: Locked or isolated medical equipment disrupted radiology and pathology departments.

facts.subject: Locked or isolated medical devices
facts.evidence: As at 19 May, NHS England had identified 1,220 infected pieces of diagnostic equipment.

facts.subject: 1220 diagnostic devices as of 19 May 2017
facts.object: About 1 percent of NHS diagnostic equipment
facts.evidence: The 1,220 infected devices were about 1% of all such NHS equipment.

facts.subject: 46 disrupted but not infected trusts
facts.evidence: NAO explicitly distinguishes the 46 trusts as not infected but reporting disruption.

facts.subject: 46 disrupted but not infected trusts
facts.object: Shutting down email and other systems
facts.evidence: Some disrupted non-infected trusts shut down email and other systems as a precaution.

facts.subject: 46 disrupted but not infected trusts
facts.evidence: NAO lists trusts disconnecting from N3 as one cause of disruption.

facts.subject: 25 infected acute trusts
facts.object: Five acute trusts diverting emergency ambulances
facts.evidence: Of the 25 infected acute trusts, five had to divert emergency ambulance services.

facts.subject: Five acute trusts diverting emergency ambulances
facts.evidence: Barts Health NHS Trust is one of the five listed diverting trusts.

facts.subject: Barts Health NHS Trust
facts.evidence: NAO lists Barts Health NHS Trust with Royal London Hospital.

facts.subject: Five acute trusts diverting emergency ambulances
facts.object: Mid Essex Hospital Services NHS Trust
facts.evidence: Mid Essex Hospital Services NHS Trust is one of the five listed diverting trusts.

facts.subject: Mid Essex Hospital Services NHS Trust
facts.evidence: NAO lists Mid Essex Hospital Services NHS Trust with Broomfield Hospital.

facts.subject: Five acute trusts diverting emergency ambulances
facts.object: East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust
facts.evidence: East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust is one of the five listed diverting trusts.

facts.subject: East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust
facts.evidence: NAO lists East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust with Lister Hospital.

facts.subject: Five acute trusts diverting emergency ambulances
facts.evidence: Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the five listed diverting trusts.

facts.subject: Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
facts.evidence: NAO lists Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust with Basingstoke Hospital.

facts.subject: Five acute trusts diverting emergency ambulances
facts.object: North Cumbria University Hospitals NHS Trust
facts.evidence: North Cumbria University Hospitals NHS Trust is one of the five listed diverting trusts.

facts.subject: North Cumbria University Hospitals NHS Trust
facts.evidence: NAO lists North Cumbria University Hospitals NHS Trust with West Cumberland Hospital.

facts.subject: Royal London Hospital
facts.evidence: The listed hospitals were diverting emergency ambulance services.

facts.subject: Broomfield Hospital
facts.evidence: The listed hospitals were diverting emergency ambulance services.

facts.subject: Lister Hospital
facts.evidence: The listed hospitals were diverting emergency ambulance services.

facts.subject: Emergency ambulance services
facts.object: Patients travelling further for emergency care
facts.evidence: Some patients had to travel further because five hospitals diverted services.

facts.subject: Patients travelling further for emergency care
facts.object: Number of diverted ambulances and patients not collected
facts.evidence: NHS England did not collect data on how many ambulances and patients were diverted.

facts.subject: Number of diverted ambulances and patients not collected
facts.object: Department and NHS England did not know full diversion count
facts.evidence: NAO says neither the Department nor NHS England knew how many ambulances and patients were diverted.

facts.subject: 6912 identified cancelled appointments
facts.evidence: NHS England identified that 6,912 appointments had been cancelled.

facts.subject: NHS England identified cancellations
facts.evidence: NHS England estimated the total number of cancelled appointments as around 19,494.

facts.subject: About 19494 estimated cancellations
facts.evidence: The estimate was based on the normal rate of follow-up appointments to first appointments.

facts.subject: Normal follow-up-to-first appointment rate
facts.evidence: NAO identifies the normal follow-up to first appointment rate as the basis for the cancellation estimate.

facts.subject: Estimate basis for total cancellations
facts.evidence: NAO says the initial 6,912 figure did not include repeat outpatient appointments.

facts.subject: Repeat outpatient appointments
facts.evidence: Repeat outpatient appointments were excluded from the initial 6,912 count.

facts.subject: Excluded from initial 6912 collection
facts.evidence: The initial 6,912 figure also excluded cancellations identified after 18 May.

facts.subject: Cancellations identified after 18 May
facts.evidence: Cancellations identified after 18 May were also outside the initial 6,912 count.

facts.subject: Also excluded from initial 6912 collection
facts.object: Actual cancelled-appointment number not planned for identification
facts.evidence: NHS England told NAO it did not plan to identify the actual cancellation number.

facts.subject: 6912 identified cancelled appointments
facts.evidence: NAO's summary figure notes the identified cancelled appointments included cancelled patient operations.

facts.subject: NHS England identified cancellations
facts.object: At least 139 urgent cancer referrals by 18 May
facts.evidence: NHS England identified at least 139 urgent referrals for potential cancer cancelled as at 18 May.

facts.subject: 603 primary care and other NHS organisations
facts.evidence: The 603 infected primary care and other organisations included 595 GP practices.

facts.subject: 595 GP practices
facts.evidence: The DHSC review says 595 infected practices needed machines rebuilt before they were patched.

facts.subject: Machines rebuilt before patching
facts.object: Re-installation and patching by IT delivery partners
facts.evidence: Commissioning Support Units and other IT delivery partners worked with NHS England and NHS Digital to re-install and patch primary-care systems.

facts.subject: Re-installation and patching by IT delivery partners
facts.evidence: The DHSC review says 95% of infected practices were re-installed and patched by 17 May.

facts.subject: 95 percent complete by 17 May 2017
facts.object: Remaining 5 percent completed by Friday 19 May 2017
facts.evidence: The remaining 5% were completed by Friday 19 May when the incident was stood down.

facts.subject: Remaining 5 percent completed by Friday 19 May 2017
facts.evidence: The remaining primary-care patching was completed by Friday 19 May when the incident was stood down.

facts.subject: Friday 19 May 2017
facts.evidence: NAO Figure 2 records the incident being stood down at 5:30 pm on Friday 19 May.

facts.subject: Incident stood down at 5:30 pm
facts.evidence: NAO records NHS England standing down the incident on Friday 19 May.

facts.subject: NHS England stand-down decision
facts.object: One-week incident period from 12 May to 19 May 2017
facts.evidence: The DHSC review says the incident lasted a week, from 16:00 on 12 May to 17:30 on 19 May.

facts.subject: Re-installation and patching by IT delivery partners
facts.evidence: The DHSC review names Commissioning Support Units among IT delivery partners involved in primary-care remediation.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: At 4 pm on 12 May, NHS England declared the cyber attack a major incident.

facts.subject: 4:00 pm on 12 May 2017
facts.evidence: The DHSC review says the incident was formally stood up at 16:00 on 12 May.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.object: Emergency Preparedness Resilience and Response plans
facts.evidence: NAO says NHS England initiated EPRR plans at 6:45 pm to act as the single point of coordination.

facts.subject: Emergency Preparedness Resilience and Response plans
facts.evidence: NAO records NHS England initiating EPRR plans at 6:45 pm on 12 May.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: Figure 2 says NHS England led the response, coordinating particularly with NHS Digital.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: NAO says the Department and NHS England worked together on the response.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: NAO lists the National Cyber Security Centre among organisations involved in the response.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: The Department, NHS England and the National Crime Agency told NAO no NHS organisation paid the ransom.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: NAO lists NHS Improvement among organisations involved in the response.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: NHS Digital wrote to all trusts on 14 May advising against ransom payments.

facts.subject: 14 May anti-ransom letter
facts.object: Do not pay the WannaCry ransom
facts.evidence: The 14 May letter advised against paying ransoms.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: The Department, NHS England and the National Crime Agency told NAO no NHS organisation paid the ransom.

facts.subject: WannaCry kill-switch
facts.evidence: A cyber-security researcher activated the kill-switch on the evening of 12 May.

facts.subject: Cyber-security researcher
facts.evidence: NAO says a cyber-security researcher activated the kill-switch.

facts.subject: WannaCry kill-switch
facts.evidence: The kill-switch meant WannaCry stopped locking devices.

facts.subject: WannaCry kill-switch
facts.evidence: The DHSC review says the kill-switch had the effect of stopping WannaCry infecting further devices.

facts.subject: Further WannaCry device locking
facts.evidence: NAO says the researcher's action meant infected organisations were not locked out and the attack could have caused more disruption otherwise.

facts.subject: NHS service recovery
facts.object: Only Lister and Broomfield still diverting by 16 May 2017
facts.evidence: By Tuesday 16 May, only Lister Hospital and Broomfield Hospital were still diverting patients.

facts.subject: Only Lister and Broomfield still diverting by 16 May 2017
facts.evidence: NAO names Lister Hospital as one of the two hospitals still diverting on 16 May.

facts.subject: Only Lister and Broomfield still diverting by 16 May 2017
facts.evidence: NAO names Broomfield Hospital as one of the two hospitals still diverting on 16 May.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: NHS England stood down the incident on Friday 19 May.

facts.subject: NHS England major incident response
facts.evidence: After WannaCry, NHS England and NHS Improvement wrote to boards seeking assurance on CareCERT alerts and firewall action.

facts.subject: Post-attack board assurance request
facts.object: 39 CareCERT alerts from March to May 2017
facts.evidence: The post-attack request asked boards to implement all 39 CareCERT alerts issued between March and May 2017.

facts.subject: Post-attack board assurance request
facts.evidence: The post-attack request also asked boards to take essential action to secure local firewalls.

facts.subject: Department of Health
facts.evidence: NAO identifies a lesson to develop and test a cyber-attack response plan with clear national and local roles.

facts.subject: Tested national cyber-attack response plan
facts.object: Clear national and local response roles
facts.evidence: The lesson was to have a response plan setting out clear roles and responsibilities for national and local organisations.

facts.subject: Department of Health
facts.object: Assurance that critical CareCERT alerts were implemented
facts.evidence: NAO lists the need to ensure organisations implement critical CareCERT alerts, including patches.
